reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown place Korah away from the swallowed tents, so that household belonged to Dathan and Abiram, leaving Korah's own sons alive.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats the Korah story as a composite narrative, later strata introducing a surviving post-exilic Levitical Korah family alongside the earlier destroyed rebel.

quotes.text: In the earlier version the princes of the tribe of Reuben were forced to give way to a prince of the tribe of Judah. In the progress of time Korah the prince of the tribe of Judah is replaced by the eponymous head of a post-exilic Levitical family, of the same name.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the composite literary strata of the Korah narrative (Numbers 16, 26).

sides.snippet: the earth opened its mouth, and swallowed them up, and their households, and all the men who appertained to Korah
sides.verseText: and the earth opened its mouth, and swallowed them up, and their households, and all the men who appertained to Korah, and all their goods.

sides.snippet: Notwithstanding, the sons of Korah didn't die.
sides.verseText: Notwithstanding, the sons of Korah didn't die.
